chunks.text: Register on the HackNova event page. Enter your email, verify it with the one-time password (OTP) we send, and fill in your college, department, year and session choices. You get a ticket with a QR code on the page and by email.
chunks.heading: How do I register?

chunks.text: Log in to the attendee portal with your email and the OTP to open your ticket again. The helpdesk at the main gate can also look up your registration if you show your college ID.
chunks.heading: I lost my ticket QR code. What do I do?

chunks.text: Check-in opens at 08:30 IST on both days at the registration desk at the main gate and closes at 10:00. Hackathon participants who stay overnight do not need to check in again on day 2, but must keep their badge on.
chunks.heading: When does check-in open?

chunks.text: Yes. When a session or the hackathon is full, you are added to the waitlist in the order you registered. If a seat frees up, you are promoted automatically and notified on your registered channel.
chunks.heading: Is there a waitlist?

chunks.text: Yes. Connect to the network HackNova-Guest. The password is printed on the back of your badge and is also available at the helpdesk.
chunks.heading: Is there WiFi?

chunks.text: Two-wheeler parking is behind Block C. There is no car parking for students on campus; cars can use the paid parking on the main road outside Gate 2.
chunks.heading: Where can I park?

chunks.text: No accommodation is provided. Hackathon participants can stay overnight in the hackathon labs and the Library reading hall on the night of 24 October. Talks and workshop attendees must leave campus by 22:00.
chunks.heading: Is accommodation provided?

chunks.text: The nearest metro station is 2 km from the campus. A free shuttle runs from the metro station to the main gate every 30 minutes from 08:00 to 10:30 and from 17:00 to 20:00 on both days.
chunks.heading: How do I get to the venue?

chunks.text: Deccan Institute students get On Duty attendance through their department; the OD list goes to HODs by 28 October. Students from other colleges can ask for an attendance letter at the helpdesk on 25 October.
chunks.heading: Do I get an OD letter?

chunks.text: Participation certificates are emailed within 7 days after the event to everyone who checked in on both days. You can check any certificate ID on the verify page.
chunks.heading: When will I get my certificate?

chunks.text: Yes. Talks and workshops are free for registered attendees, and you do not need to join the hackathon to attend them. Workshop seats are limited, so pick your sessions during registration.
chunks.heading: Can I attend only the workshops?

chunks.text: Participants must be 18 or older, or confirm that a parent or guardian has given consent during registration.
chunks.heading: Is there an age limit?

chunks.text: Lost and found is at the helpdesk next to the registration desk at the main gate.
chunks.heading: Where is the lost and found?

chunks.text: Yes. The first aid room is Room G-12 on the ground floor of Block A, staffed throughout the event. An ambulance is on call. In an emergency, tell any volunteer immediately.
chunks.heading: Is there medical help on campus?

chunks.text: Every hackathon lab has power strips at each table. The auditorium has charging points along the side walls. Power backup covers all labs.
chunks.heading: Can I charge my laptop and phone?

chunks.text: Visit the helpdesk at the main gate, ask any volunteer in a HackNova T-shirt, or write to help@example.com.
chunks.heading: How do I contact the organisers?

chunks.text: Use the "delete my data" option in the attendee portal. Personal data is deleted 90 days after the event unless you have requested a certificate.
chunks.heading: How do I delete my data?

chunks.text: All meals are served at the Food Court in Block D. Food is not served inside the auditorium or the labs. Your ticket QR code is your meal coupon; show it at the counter.
chunks.heading: HackNova 2026 Food and Menu

chunks.text: - Breakfast, 08:00 to 09:30: idli, vada, sambar, poha, tea and coffee. - Lunch, 12:30 to 14:00: veg biryani, chicken biryani, paneer butter masala, dal, rice, curd, and gulab jamun. - Evening snacks, 16:30 to 17:30: samosa and tea. - Dinner, 20:00 to 21:30, for hackathon participants only: chapati, veg kurma, chilli chicken, jeera rice and ice cream. - Midnight snacks, 00:30: Maggi, sandwiches, tea and coffee, for hackathon participants.
chunks.heading: Day 1: Saturday 24 October

chunks.text: - Breakfast, 07:30 to 09:00: upma, dosa, chutney, tea and coffee. - Lunch, 12:30 to 14:00: veg pulao, egg curry, dal tadka, rice, curd and fruit salad.
chunks.heading: Day 2: Sunday 25 October

chunks.text: Every meal has a vegetarian option. Jain meals are available if you selected Jain as your food preference during registration. Vegan options are available at lunch on request at the counter.
chunks.heading: Dietary options

chunks.text: The Day 1 lunch dessert (gulab jamun) contains dairy, and the Day 1 dinner ice cream contains nuts. Ask the counter staff for the allergen card for any dish.
chunks.heading: Allergens

chunks.text: A tea and coffee counter runs 24 hours during the hackathon on the Block B second floor, near Lab 204. Drinking water refill stations are on every floor; bring your own bottle.
chunks.heading: Drinks

chunks.text: HackNova 2026 is a two-day tech fest with a 24-hour hackathon, held on 24 and 25 October 2026 at Deccan Institute of Engineering and Technology, Hyderabad.

The hackathon is open to undergraduate and postgraduate students from any college. Participants must be 18 or older, or confirm guardian consent during registration. A valid college ID card is mandatory at check-in and must be worn at all times on campus.
chunks.heading: Eligibility

chunks.text: Teams have 2 to 4 members. A person can be part of only one team. Team members can be changed until 18:00 IST on 23 October 2026 from the registration portal. After that, team composition is frozen. Solo participation is not allowed in the hackathon, but solo attendees are welcome at talks and workshops.
chunks.heading: Teams

chunks.text: The hackathon starts at 10:00 IST on 24 October and ends at 10:00 IST on 25 October. Final submissions must be made on the submission portal before 10:00 IST on 25 October. Late submissions are not accepted. Shortlisted teams present to judges from 11:30 to 14:30 on 25 October, and results are announced at the closing ceremony at 16:00 in the Main Auditorium.
chunks.heading: Hackathon timeline

chunks.text: There are three tracks: AI and ML, Web and Cloud, and Hardware and IoT. Each team picks one track at registration and can change it until the hackathon starts.
chunks.heading: Tracks

chunks.text: Projects are scored out of 100: innovation 30 points, technical depth 30 points, impact 20 points, and presentation 20 points. Judges' decisions are final.
chunks.heading: Judging criteria

chunks.text: First prize is 50,000 INR, second prize is 30,000 INR, and third prize is 15,000 INR. There is also a Best Women-led Team prize of 10,000 INR. Prize money is transferred to the team leader's bank account within 30 days after the event.
chunks.heading: Prizes

chunks.text: All project code must be written during the hackathon. Open-source libraries and public APIs are allowed with attribution in the README. AI coding assistants are allowed, but their use must be disclosed in the submission. Reusing a project built before the event leads to disqualification.
chunks.heading: Code and tools

chunks.text: Harassment of any kind is not tolerated. Report any incident to a volunteer in a HackNova T-shirt or at the helpdesk; reports are handled confidentially by the organising committee. Alcohol, smoking and vaping are prohibited on campus. Violations can lead to removal from the event without refund.
chunks.heading: Conduct

chunks.text: Bring your own laptop and chargers. The Hardware and IoT track gets a shared kit (Arduino, ESP32, sensors) issued against a college ID at the Lab 101 counter; kits must be returned before 12:00 on 25 October.
chunks.heading: Hardware

chunks.text: Mentors are available in the hackathon labs from 12:00 to 20:00 on 24 October and from 07:00 to 09:30 on 25 October. Book a slot at the mentor desk outside Lab 204.
chunks.heading: Mentors

chunks.text: All participants who check in on both days receive a participation certificate by email within 7 days after the event. Winners receive merit certificates. Every certificate has an ID that can be checked on the public verify page. Students of Deccan Institute get On Duty (OD) attendance through their department: the OD list is sent to HODs by 28 October. Students from other colleges can request an attendance letter at the helpdesk on 25 October.
chunks.heading: Certificates and OD

chunks.text: The hackathon registration fee is 200 INR per person. Talks and workshops are free for registered attendees. Fees are non-refundable, except when the organisers cancel the event, in which case the full fee is refunded within 14 days.
chunks.heading: Fees and refunds

chunks.text: - Main Auditorium: Block A, ground floor, 400 seats. Keynotes, opening at 09:30 on 24 October, and the closing ceremony at 16:00 on 25 October. - Lab 204: Block B, second floor, 60 seats. AI and ML track workshops and hackathon teams. - Lab 101: Block B, first floor, 80 seats. Web and Cloud track, and the hardware kit counter. - Seminar Hall 3: Block C, first floor, 120 seats. Hardware and IoT track talks and panel discussions.
chunks.heading: Rooms

chunks.text: Block A is straight ahead from the main gate. Block B is to the left of Block A, connected by a covered walkway. Block C is behind Block B. The Food Court is in Block D, next to the parking area.
chunks.heading: Getting around

chunks.text: Wheelchair ramps are at the entrances of Block A and Block B. Block B has a lift near the main staircase that reaches every floor. Accessible washrooms are on the ground floor of Block A and Block B. Seminar Hall 3 in Block C is reachable by a ramp from the Block B walkway. Tell the registration desk if you need help moving between blocks, and a volunteer will accompany you.
chunks.heading: Accessibility

chunks.text: Washrooms are on every floor of every block. Drinking water refill stations are on every floor. A quiet room for rest is in Room C-105, and a prayer room is in Room C-104. The helpdesk and registration desk are at the main gate.
chunks.heading: Facilities

chunks.text: Campus gates open at 08:00 on both days. Non-hackathon attendees must leave by 22:00. Hackathon participants may stay overnight in the Block B labs and the Library reading hall on 24 October. Only Gate 1 (main gate) is open after 20:00.
chunks.heading: Timings and access

chunks.text: Hackathon teams work in Lab 204, Lab 101 and the Block B second floor corridor. The Library reading hall on the first floor of Block D is open overnight for rest.
chunks.heading: Hackathon spaces

chunks.text: The first aid room is Room G-12, ground floor, Block A. Fire exits are marked on every floor, and the assembly point is the main lawn in front of Block A.
chunks.heading: Safety
